title: Prompts and Conversation Context · Level 3
slo: Distinguish prompt types and explain how a model continues a conversation.

options.rationale: Prompt engineering is the practice of designing prompts to improve responses. Both the model and the prompt affect quality.
Retrieval augmented generation adds retrieved information to a prompt. It is not the general practice of designing prompts.
Behavior rules are set with a system prompt. Prompt engineering improves prompt wording and structure.
Next-token prediction is how a decoder generates a completion. It is not how a person designs a prompt.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Prompt engineering designs prompts for better results.

exercises.question_text: Which can be set by a system prompt? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Tone is part of the broad guidance a system prompt can establish. It can apply across responses.

options.text: A rule the model must follow
options.rationale: Constraints are rules for model behavior. A system prompt can set them.

options.text: A specific request for a summary
options.rationale: A summary request asks for one particular response. That is a user-prompt function.
Earlier messages are conversation history. They provide context, not behavior rules.

exercises.explanation: Correct. System prompts can set tone and constraints.

exercises.question_text: Response quality depends on both the language model and the prompts submitted to it.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A vague prompt may still yield an unhelpful result.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Response quality depends on both the model and the submitted prompt.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Better prompt design can improve a capable model's results.

exercises.question_text: A system prompt is normally the human user's specific question for the model.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Broad rules and one-time requests would be confused.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: System prompts set behavior; user prompts ask for specific responses.

exercises.explanation: Correct. A specific human question is a user prompt.

exercises.question_text: What gives a follow-up question context from an earlier chat?

options.rationale: Conversation history includes earlier prompts and responses with later prompts. It gives follow-up questions ongoing context.
A system prompt sets behavior, tone, and constraints. It does not carry prior-chat details.
A user prompt is the new question or instruction. It does not itself preserve prior discussion.
options.better_fit: It fits asking the follow-up question.

options.rationale: Masked attention is a decoder-training technique. It does not preserve chat messages.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Conversation history provides prior context.

exercises.question_text: Which statements describe masked attention? Select all that apply.

options.text: It ignores tokens after the current token
options.rationale: Masked attention hides tokens after the current position. This keeps predictions based on earlier tokens.

options.text: It is used while training the decoder
options.rationale: Masked attention is used during decoder training on complete sequences. The known next token can then be used for comparison.

options.text: It sets response tone and constraints
options.rationale: Tone and constraints are response guidance. Masked attention is a decoder-training technique.
Retrieval adds information to a prompt. Masked attention hides future tokens during training.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Masked attention hides later tokens during decoder training.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The follow-up may be answered without its needed topic.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: First discuss a topic, then ask a follow-up and include the earlier context.

exercises.correct_answer: Discuss a topic Ask a follow-up Include earlier context Answer stays relevant
exercises.explanation: An earlier discussion gives a follow-up its context when that context is included.

exercises.question_text: After comparing a prediction with the known next token, training adjusts the model's ___ to reduce error over later iterations.

parts.text: After comparing a prediction with the known next token, training adjusts the model's
to reduce error over later iterations.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The sentence would not identify what training changes to improve future predictions.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Training updates learned weights after measuring prediction error.

exercises.explanation: Masked-attention training compares predictions with known targets and adjusts learned weights to reduce error.

exercises.question_text: The decoder repeatedly selects the most probable next ___ in a sequence.

parts.text: The decoder repeatedly selects the most probable next

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The missing term would not name the item added to the sequence.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: A token is the unit predicted next.

exercises.explanation: A decoder builds a completion by predicting one token at a time.

options.rationale: A user prompt asks for a response to a particular question or instruction. It is input to the model.

options.text: Overall behavior set by an app
options.rationale: Overall behavior is broad guidance. A user prompt instead asks for a particular response.
A record of earlier messages is conversation history. It provides context for later prompts.
A predicted token is generated in a completion. A user prompt is model input.

exercises.explanation: Correct. A user prompt is a specific request.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the steps of next-token prediction.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The next prediction would lack the newly generated context.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Predict, add the token, then use the expanded sequence until an end is predicted.

exercises.correct_answer: Predict a token Add it to sequence Use expanded sequence Stop at sequence end
exercises.explanation: The predicted token is added to the sequence, which becomes context for the next prediction.

exercises.question_text: A person or an application can create a user prompt.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Valid application-created requests would be overlooked.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: User prompts may be created by a person or by an application.

exercises.explanation: Correct. An application can generate a user prompt on a person's behalf.
